identity.title: Bounded rejection of one fixed junk asset in a continuation

explanation.summary: Check whether the reference linear-vesting program explicitly rejects a valid Claim context after adding one unit of the fixed zzzzjunk/zzzzjunk asset to its first continuation under four guards.
explanation.claim: For the selected Claim model, quantify over its leaves, r : TxOutRef, and a : Int. The mutation appends an input at unrelatedKey funding the lovelace amount a and one unit of zzzzjunk/zzzzjunk. It appends a separate output at unrelatedKey returning that lovelace and appends the junk asset to only the first continuation's value. The quantified a is lovelace, not token quantity or count. Require baseline validScriptContext, baseline acceptance, explicit rejection after redirectContinuations, and validScriptContext after addJunkFrom. Under these four premises, the changed context must explicitly reject. A separate applicability obligation requires a witness to all four premises. Acceptance and explicit rejection use 1,000,000 CEK steps; rejection means an error or a non-unit halt, and fuel exhaustion does not count.
explanation.purpose: Preserve the original guarded Claim rejection and applicability formulas through the native property workflow. Both obligations retain the expected result Valid; reproducing the historical original Claim pair of Falsified rejection and Valid applicability yields an official FAIL.

relevance_conditions: Relevant to the Claim action of the reference linear-vesting compiled artifact within TxM-007.
The property requires rejection after a combined address-and-datum redirection. That guard does not independently prove reliance on a continuation's value or rejection of extra assets.
preconditions: The target is the exact reference compiled artifact in Formal.TxModels.Artifacts.LinearVesting.referenceCompiledCode and is an unparameterized Plutus V3 spending program.
The original modeled context satisfies validScriptContext.
The supplied program accepts the original context within 1,000,000 CEK steps.
The supplied program explicitly rejects redirectContinuations of the original context within the same bound.
The context changed by addJunkFrom still satisfies validScriptContext.
limitations: The shared TxM-007 model admits two compiler artifacts. UP-008 restricts this binding to the original reference artifact and skips the second artifact without generating proof obligations.
Only Claim is bound to the native workflow. The retained standalone Cancel model has no continuation and an inapplicable applicability observation; its implication supplies no mutation coverage.

Claim has two inputs and two outputs: a script continuation with an inline datum followed by a signer payout. It uses one signer, one vested asset under fixed policyA, key credentials in the original vesting datum, no constructed staking credentials, and a finite lower validity bound with no upper bound. Reference inputs, minting, and withdrawals are absent. Symbolic leaves vary within this fixed geometry.

The mutation appends an input identified by r at unrelatedKey holding the lovelace amount a and one unit of the fixed asset whose policy and name are both zzzzjunk. It appends an output at unrelatedKey returning the lovelace and appends the fixed junk asset to the first continuation's value. The changed Claim has three inputs and three outputs. The quantified a : Int is lovelace, not a token quantity or count; the junk quantity is always one. The unrelatedKey bytes remain 756e72656c61746564.

Continuations are identified by payment-credential equality with the spent input, without comparing staking credentials. Only the first matching output's value changes. Its address, datum, and reference script are preserved, as are all original inputs, all other original outputs, and all other context fields. This does not establish arbitrary output-order coverage or multiple-continuation coverage.

The redirect guard instead changes every matching output's entire address to keyAddr attackerKey and removes its datum. The fixed attackerKey bytes remain 61747461636b6572. Rejection after these combined changes does not independently prove reliance on continuation value or rejection of extra assets.

The primary statement retains exactly the original four premises. Applicability separately requires a context, input reference r, and lovelace amount a satisfying all four. The changed-context validity guard controls admissible references, values, and transaction bookkeeping; no new guard or configurable token-count policy is added.
The script credential p.script remains symbolic and is not constrained to the supplied program's hash.

The historical original Claim result is Falsified rejection with Valid applicability. Both native obligations still expect Valid, so reproducing that pair yields an official FAIL. That artifact/model result does not by itself establish token flooding, locked funds, a vulnerability, or a configurable token-count limit.

The frozen compiled enforcing control remains test-only. It checks that the first continuation contains zero units of exactly zzzzjunk/zzzzjunk, not the number of token entries. Its checks preserve the complete Claim model, fixed mutation, all four guards, symbolic script credential, and fuel while changing only the evaluated program. It is not admitted by this native binding.
These checks concern the fixed model and pinned program. They do not establish arbitrary transaction coverage, full ledger reachability, deployment exposure, or general validator safety.
The check adds no requirement that every output contain at least 1 ADA and does not print a transaction witness.
Acceptance and explicit rejection use 1,000,000 CEK steps. Rejection requires an error or a non-unit halt; fuel exhaustion does not count. This bound is not a ledger CPU or memory budget.
A primary rejection result needs the separate applicability result to exclude vacuity under the selected model. A timeout or solver error leaves the affected obligation unresolved.

Successful generated Blaster checks retain the blasterProven SMT trust assumption. This metadata preserves historical observations and the property definition; it does not assert a new target-specific proof result.
The configurable limit on distinct output tokens and broader asset/model coverage in issue #29, and broader workflow integration and follow-up work in issue #96, remain open.
